title: Distributed tracing: Jaeger, Zipkin, and the trace that crosses a queue

videos.script: Lessons 2 to 4 built traces. This lesson reads them, in the two open-source stores that started the field. Jaeger, and Zipkin before it. {{stores}} You take one slow checkout and work out where its time went, span by span, separating the time a span spent working from the time it spent waiting for others. {{self}} You search for every slow checkout of the last three minutes. You ask Zipkin which services call which, and how often. {{search}} Then the queue. The mailer stops for thirty seconds while customers keep buying, and the traces measure how long each confirmation waited. {{queue}} And finally the link lesson 1 promised. A latency histogram that carries, beside its counts, the id of a real request that landed in each bucket. {{exemplar}}
